newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodian border conflict boosts Thai rice trade.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian border conflict boosts Thai rice trade.

text.p: Demand for rice along the Thai-Cambodian border has risen sharply with fighting in Cambodia forcing thousands of civilians to flee into Thailand, a trader said on Tuesday.
A trader in this Thai northeastern border province told Reuters that his mill could sell up to eight tonnes of rice a day through relief agencies such as the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees.

"Based on the current situation, I would think the relief agencies will need to buy rice from Thailand to supply to Cambodia for at least another two to three months," said Kriangkai, an official at the Sin-Udom rice mill, the biggest in Surin.
"Our mill supplies an average of 80 tonnes per week through auctions," he said.
Kriangkai did not give details but said current rice prices were very high.
"In my whole life, I have never seen the rice price go up this high. The paddy we bought for milling normally cost around six to seven baht a kg. But now it has topped 10 baht," he said.

More than 20,000 Cambodian civilians, most of them women and children, have fled into Thailand from O'Smach -- the last stronghold of troops loyal to ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh who are fighting forces loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
